text_fidelity_a:
AKAMATE Active Noise Cancelling Headphones, Wireless Neckband Headset Bluetooth V4.2 in-Ear Waterproof Earbuds Magnetic Hi-Fi Stereo Sports Earphones with Mic, Carrying Bag There is always a run on headphones in our house. Not only are they being lost or dying, but everyone is on a constant quest for the best design and sound they can find in a bluetooth headphone. Let's see how these measure up.

WHAT ARE THESE HEADPHONES LIKE?
These headphones have a long sturdy neck band which means they will fit a variety of neck sizes. Each ear piece has a magnet on it so that when you are not using them, they will close in front of you so you won't lose them. The controls are at the end of the neck band on the right side.

ON/OFF BUTTON
Play, pause, on/off, pair can be done with this button.

VOLUME
The minus and plus of volume control is also used for skipping songs- + skip forward, - skip backward.

ANC
There is an ANC button on the right side directly behind the negative volume button which makes it easy to press them both at the same time. It does do noise canceling, but it is frustrating because it is easy to press the ANC button by mistake when also pressing the middle button.

CHARGING PORT
Charging port is on the edge of the control button area.

AI INDICATOR VOICE
The automatic voice is very dysfunctional. It only says part of words, and seems to be a bit mean sounding which makes my daughter say it feels creepy.

NOISE CANCELING
The noise canceling works beautifully on these headphones.

SOUND QUALITY
The sound quality is awesome. Highs and mids are where they should be. Bass is very good. It is not overdone but it is in balance and does not distract from the music. There are not any breakups in sound unless you walk away from the device.

BLUETOOTH RANGE
The bluetooth range seems to be good up to about 35 feet or so.

PHONE CALL QUALITY
The calls go through very well and people can hear just fine on phone calls.

BATTERY PERCENTAGE
There is no physical light indicator to tell you how much battery power you have left.

THE BOTTOM LINE
If you want a good solid set of headphones to use with phone and music that work well, are in balance, and great for listening. The controls are not as convenient as they could be, which can be frustrating at times.

MY RATING
Four stars. If the control area was set up just a little more conveniently so that you can not accidentally press the wrong buttons all of the time, they would probably be five stars.
text_fidelity_b: AKAMATE Active Noise Cancelling Headphones, Wireless Neckband Headset Bluetooth V4.2 in-Ear Waterproof Earbuds Magnetic Hi-Fi Stereo Sports Earphones with Mic, Carrying Bag

text_fidelity_a:
Lexar JumpDrive S47 128GB USB 3.1 Flash Drive (LJDS47-128ABBKNA) I have had a need for an additional storage solution for my laptop which will enable me to back up files, and transfer between desktop (my workstation) and my laptop when necessary. My goal is to have it as an alternative mini hard drive, so to speak. Let's take a Look.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This is a tiny Jumpdrive, for those who have never used one, it is similar in appearance to a dongle that you use for wireless keyboard or mouse in the USB port. It does not have a case and the packaging is rather difficult to open.

WHAT IS THIS FOR?
This is designed not to carry with you all of the time like some of the flash drives, but to use almost as a mini hard drive and keep it in your laptop or even desktop if desired. It will keep your files handy, has a pretty fast transfer rate, and has a decent amount of storage, depending on what kind of files you plan to store on it.

WHAT ELSE CAN YOU USE THESE FOR?
This can also be theoretically used to keep in the car as a way to play music on your sound system via USB port. I have not been able to do that yet as I have had some issues setting up the right format. I am not sure how security will interact with that..

DOES THIS HAVE SECURITY ON IT?
This drive has a program called ENCDataVault Lite. That will allow you to encrypt your files and have them accessed with a password you set up in case you lose your drive at least your files will be somewhat protected unless it is a hacker who finds it.

HOW IS TRANSFER RATE?
I have used this in a USB3.0 as well as USB2.0 port and both worked well.

DOES THIS FIT TYPE C CONNECTION?
You can not use this in a type C port so please check your laptop or desktop prior to purchase to be sure you have an actual USB port to use this in that is not already being used.

WHAT I DON'T LIKE ABOUT THIS
This drive should come with a tiny case on a keychain or with at least a loop handle on it so that you can put it somewhere safe and not lose it. It does not come with that. Something this small needs to have a colorful case to make it harder to lose. I know that the idea is to have it stay in the unit you use it on mostly, but sometimes you have to take it out and it needs a case.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a tiny drive. It is meant to use in either a car sound system (USB port), on a laptop or desktop that you plan to use it on regularly, and not be moved around constantly. It does not come with any kind of case at all to store it in when not in a port. It does have encryption which is a big plus to theoretically protect files in case of loss.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. The performance is top notch. The fact that this does not come with a case is worth removing a star. Ideally it would not be a problem most of the time, but I still think that it needs protective COLORFUl case for those times you need to remove it from a port and take it from one place to another.
text_fidelity_b: Lexar JumpDrive S47 128GB USB 3.1 Flash Drive (LJDS47-128ABBKNA)

text_fidelity_a:
Sony ICFC218 Dream Machine Clock Radio (Black) This is not a bad clock radio for the price I paid. It's not a great one either, but it fit the profile of what I wanted with one exception, which I'll get to in a bit.

First off, it's smallish, which is a blessing on a crowded nightstand. The display seems fine to me, neither too bright, nor too dim. It's easy to program, thank goodness. I've had a lot of electronics that require three hands, and a stopwatch to be properly programmed. The ICF-C218 has a button or a dial for each function. Just follow the instructions and you'll be fine. It's a bit hard to see the radio dial unless you pick it up, but that's a minor thing for someone like me, who pretty much keeps it on one station. It's not programmable; you have to change the station with a tuning dial. However the reception is excellent, even without an external antenna.

My quibble, and it's a relatively small one, is that the sound is tinny. I don't expect a lot out of a small radio like this, but I have a Sangean which is even smaller, and the sound is much better. It's not a deal-breaker, I got what I wanted in every other respect.

Bottom line: Good price point for a basic clock radio with excellent reception, and so-so sound.
text_fidelity_b: Sony ICFC218 Dream Machine Clock Radio (Black)

text_fidelity_a: Ring Floodlight Cam Wired Plus with motion-activated 1080p HD video, White (2021 release) I already had the doorbell pro cam, 3 indoor stick up cams, and an outdoor cam for my pool.  When our spotlight above our garage door went out, we were going to buy a new light but because our driveway is not visible on my doorbell cam we decided to try this.  My house was built in 1983, and I think the outdoor spot light there was original.  It was completely rusted.  I questioned whether or not this would actually work.  But it did,  it hooked right up, I didn’t have to order anything else,  the original mounting fixture worked and it is completely water proof.  Now, this light is controlled with a light switch, so, if anyone turns it off the power to the cam is cut off.  But I’m going to put a piece of tape over it.  I was able to set the parameters so that it didn’t pick up every car going down the road, just cars that pulled into my driveway.  And the light does come on automatically at night, and it is bright bright.  The voices coming through seem to be clearer than my older cameras.  Also, even though my Wi-Fi router is upstairs on the other side of the house it’s picking up signal good and haven’t had an issue there.  This literally took like 30 minutes to install and get it running on my ring app.  I was pretty surprised.  I’m glad I bit the bullet and purchased this instead of a regular light.

You can't use the left alone. I was so shocked at such a huge technology failure on bose's part, why in the world would they make the decision to have half the product be useless?

You can only do this with the right bud!
All the other nice headphones I listed do not do this. The last pair of headphones that connected the right to the phone and the left to the right was a $30 pair of skull candies.
This is absolutely not "top of the line".
Some days I'll wear one headphone for 10-12 hrs while doing chores and errands. With these, I can wear the right one until it dies, then I have nothing until it charges....

I'm so disappointed because I really love the fit and quality, but for the price tag, I'm going to return them.
Bose needs to fix this outdated ridiculous low quality crap.
If you need the left one to connect by itself then steer clear of Bose.

text_fidelity_a:
NETGEAR 8-Port Ultra60 PoE Multi-Gigabit Ethernet Plus Switch (MS108EUP) - Managed, with 4 x PoE++ and 4 x PoE+ @ 230W, Desktop or Wall Mount, and Limited Lifetime Protection I received this item through the Amazon Vine program, although the usual green writing may not be shown. The review is specifically for model: GS305EPP.

Port Binding: I noticed that the Netgear chart shows for the "plus" series of switches, that only models with 16 or more ports support port binding. However, through the web interface, I was able to do a single instance of port binding (it looks like it allows you to bind up to four ports, although I can't think of an instance where binding more than two ports on a five port switch would be worthwhile). I learned some quirks about port binding in the process, that using 802.3ad with multiple Linux servers doesn't allow for more than a Gb of data in any one direction anyway. BUT this switch does apparently support balance-rr, because I could get almost 2Gb/s over a 2Gb aggregate link. I think my hard drives in those machines were maxed out at that point. As I understand it, balance-rr has a high error rate because it uses striping and not all machines support it. But it was working quite nicely with my NAS units and this switch (I was expecting the 8 port switch, which would have made that setup more worthwhile because I could fatten the links on all three servers.

Although my current Netgear Pro AP does not have two ports for binding, I did have an AP before that supported it, in which case that feature on this switch may be an excellent option (particularly considering it is PoE). I haven't done the math for myself, but I think that port binding is almost a gimmick on APs because there is so much overhead on WiFi that even if your AP has a throughput in the multi-Gb range, enough of that is overhead created by the AP that you're not actually getting that much data from one computer to another.

Insight and Web Interface: The Insight App shows this switch (and my Netgear APs) as having "limited support" (just shows basic device info and a link to the device's webpage), so they're not really trying to get users of the "plus" line to subscribe to that in perpetuity.

And you don't need the app to use the switch. You don't even need the configuration page, really: I just plugged this into my old 24-port unmanaged Netgear workhose and it picked up an IP from the router and worked just like an unmanaged switch until I decided to give it a static IP and manage it.

I was really surprised how many features are packed into the management software, considering these are Netgear's lower line of managed devices. But most of the stuff you'll see on huge enterprise devices is here as well (well, it's been a while since I've been inside the big enterprise stuff, but all those goodies reach us as consumers before long).

The web interface is just like any other network device - you can reach it from any webpage and it is super GUI - probably just a little more than I really want it to be, but it is very intuitive and you can find everything with a few clicks. I say "super GUI" just because it looks fancier than I need it to. And one thing I find a little irritating is that when you expand one box, it collapses another, so you can't look at everything at once. This doesn't really matter, but I'm old school where I just want substance over style and even style that doesn't sacrifice substance still looks like they're trying too hard.

PoE: Clearly, on this 4+1 port switch, all four of your devices can use a full 30w each, so this is non-blocking in PoE+ as well as throughput. At time of writing, the 8 port with the same power budget was actually cheaper, so you might consider that, even if you can't use all the ports at full PoE.

What is great about this, is that besides just being able to add APs and IP cameras to your network (or even lighting, etc.), you can turn them on and off from the web interface. So I can keep my main AP on PoE (and therefore on my telecom closet's backup power supply), and then turn my detached garage's AP on and off from the web interface rather than having to go down to the basement and plug or unplug the PoE injector every time I want to use the garage AP (I just turn it on if I'm going to be working out there and might need to watch some "how-to" videos or control my audio system from the local LAN).

*Netgear, if you're listening, I would love to have a super lightweight (and free) app that works remotely (when not necessarily on LAN) to turn ports on and off for exactly this type of reason.*

Construction: Solid device, very dense and professional looking. Plenty of lights that tell you a lot from a glance. Power supply is external and about as big as the device itself. Would personally love a way to rack mount this AND the power supply (for maximum flexibility) in 1 RU, but of course I realize most people don't want to waste a whole rack unit on 5 ports. But for the space both pieces take up, it's about a mid size unit that could be mounted with "wings". It does have four-way keyhole mounts for wall-mounting.

Background: I have great experience with Netgear for my home (but way better than most homes') network. I'd definitely use all their devices were I doing work for small or medium sized businesses. I like them just a tad less when they start trying to sell you subscriptions (which is what I hate about Brocade and Cisco, along with all the proprietary garbage), but for the most part, Netgear is inexpensive and quite reliable. I've had a 24 port nonblocking unmanaged Gb switch running 24/7 in my dusty basement for over 15 years without a single fault AND they still sell that model. Their APs are the best I've had, and I don't think I've ever had a Netgear item break on me, period. I have had lots of other home/SMB stuff break or otherwise have strange issues, though.

That said, there's a lot of no-name PoE switches on the market right now. I don't need any of those handling my low voltage needs OR my data. And they won't beat this line on the price by too much anyway.

This is an excellent device which adds a lot of versatility to your network.

text_fidelity_a:
Lowepro LP36915 ViewPoint CS 40 - A Soft-Sided Protective Case for a Smartphone, GoPro or 360 Camera and Accessories,Black Reviewed by my husband, a photography enthusiast.

Over the last 20 years, my husband has purchased several LowePro camera bags/backpacks (i.e., Mini Trekker & Micro-Trekker 100). He has found that they have been some of the best he has ever owned. He prefers backpacks because they are easy to carry and keep up with, especially if you are on the go. Backpacks also allow for easy storage and are super convenient. They give you freedom of movement and your hands are free to capture those special moments that you may not otherwise get if you were holding a bag in your hand. The Viewpoint (LowePro) BP 250 is the perfect addition to his bag collection especially since it is specially designed for small video equipment.

Here’s what he liked:

• This bag is attractive. The design is smart, functional and full of surprises. The Viewpoint BP250 is well-made with plenty of room for your Go Pro and accompanying equipment. There is a ton of storage (inside and out). There are several compartments where you can store your accessories, cords, lenses and other equipment. On the outside of the main bag, there is a zipper pocket (which allows for small items like a memory stick/card or thumbdrive). There is a pocket on the other side of the bag which will fit a small tripod or other item (like an umbrella). The entire bag can be zippered so you won’t lose any of your accessories.

• It is ideal for those who use (small) video and other digital equipment. There is a space dedicated to a small computer. While this backpack will not allow you to carry one of the larger sized laptops (our 17” didn’t fit), it has adequate space for the smaller ones (about 15”), a SurfacePro, iPad or other small notebook or tablet. He finds that the option of carrying a computer is great because it will allow you to quickly upload and edit your videos wherever you are. There is no reason to wait….just review, edit (if needed), and upload!

• The straps are unlike the traditional ones that come straight down the shoulders. The BP250 LowePro’s straps are curved which he found to be less stress on his shoulders. After some adjustments (he’s 6’1, average sized with average shoulders), it was a good fit. The straps are slightly padded and comfortable. There are small snaps that lock the straps in place to ensure that they don’t fall down when walking or hiking.

• There is a small (lunch box sized bag) that can be removed and can hold your GoPro camera and equipment. Once closed, it fits directly into your main LowePro Bag. It is padded and once inside, will protect your camera and smaller lenses. Or if you want, this smaller bag can be used instead of taking the large one.

• This bag comes with a rain cover. Not sure how much you will use this feature, but if you are ever caught in a drizzle or rain storm, there is a plastic cover that can be removed (unzipped) from the bottom and cover your bag. This is perfect for keeping your bag and equipment dry.

• The price. While this bag may seem a little pricey (about $130) it’s worth it. The craftsmanship and functionality will prove invaluable for the amateur or professional photographer. It’s a small investment with some heavy returns. You’ve got protection and functionality.

Overall, my husband gives this bag 5 stars. He finds that it is not only good to use for a GoPro, but other small video and photography equipment. Backpacks are useful for photographers because they allow your hands to be free to capture those moments or events as they unfold. In the past he has purchased Lowepro equipment and found them to be sturdy and durable, and the Viewpoint BP250 is not different. It looks good and he won’t leave home without it.
text_fidelity_b: Lowepro LP36915 ViewPoint CS 40 - A Soft-Sided Protective Case for a Smartphone, GoPro or 360 Camera and Accessories,Black

We've been grabbing a few of these mini pcs to test them out and see if they're good for Distance Learning. We have a lot of spare pc peripherals including old school 4:3 screens. But for many, an all in one chromebook or cheap laptop is still infinitely more convenient. But if you do have these accessories laying around, and you're curious how this Minix works for Distance Learning, I'm happy to report it's great! I just reviewed a Beelink mini pc that is very capable too.

The 1080p camera, microphone, speakers and monitor connected with no issues. Windows did all the firmware work. The only software we had to fetch was Logitech's unifying receiver for the keyboard and mouse. In California, many k12 schools are using CLASSLINK and GOOGLE CLASS. I went into my child's account, played around with all the apps. Opened and closed browsers, everything was pretty snappy.

It's mind-boggling that Windows 10 Pro is $200 alone. Of course if you're going to pay full price for Windows 10 pro, you wouldn't put it in a low end computer. Nevertheless, it is awesome that it's included here. I recently reviewed the Beelink T4 which has the Z8500 cpu. On paper, that's slightly a faster cpu, but interestingly, the Z8350 in the Minix is a newer cpu. They may have made the Z8350 more efficient or something. In any case, normal human beings won't be able to tell the difference. LOL! The MINIX Z83-4 Plus is a little bigger than the Beelink T4, but comes with a wifi antennae, and a built in micro SD reader.

Basic activities such as web browsing, watching Netlfix, Youtube, kids doing work on ClassLink, etc., this mini pc is very capable.

SAIJI Tablet Stand Holder, Adjustable Phone Stand, 360° Rotating Portable Monitor Stand, Aluminum Alloy Cradle Desktop Holder Dock for 4.7"-15.6" Screen Phones, iPad, Nintendo Switch, Kindle(Black) 3.5 STARS. I rounded up because it is more good then bad:
Bought as a Christmas gift for the boyfriend. We are long distance and we FaceTime a lot. Well, actually, I FaceTime with the underside of his kitchen cabinets, the blanket on his bed, the ceilings in all his rooms, or the top of his nightstand. He talks away, oblivious until I say something. It's funny mostly but sometimes in a relationship you need all the connection you can get, even if it's their face on your device while they smile or laugh or talk you through a bad moment. So, I got him this for Christmas so that he could hands-free me and I could still see his pretty face. He finally put it together and started using it the other day... with an asterisk. *THE INCLUDED SCREW/BOLT IS GARBAGE. It was machined badly. Really badly. So it only screws maybe halfway into the arm/neck or whatever it is called, which sits in the weighted base. Thankfully he really doesn't need the screw/bolt because the arm/neck (like a metal dowel, I suppose, that inserts into the base maybe half an inch. The screw/bolt is inserted from under the base and - if it fits correctly) recesses into the base when it's tightened. As this one had threads that weren't smooth about halfway down on the screw/bolt, it left the screw/bolt jutted out. The base won't sit on the nightstand or other flat surface with this issue unless he just doesn't use the screw/bolt. I'd post a photo for clarification but the stand isn't available and getting him to send photos isn't always something I remember when we do talk.

The screw/bolt is I'm sure metric and it does use an Allen wrench (included) to screw in; the threading is very tight, so finding a true replacement screw/bolt is probably gonna require going to a specialty nuts/bolts/hardware store. That's annoying enough to take off 1.5 stars for me.

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm Instax Mini 26 + Rainbow Film Bundle - Black A long time ago I had access to a Polaroid Instamatic camera. It was great - snap a picture, it spits out a sheet. Wait about 2 minutes and what you have is a printed photograph. Polaroid is gone now (though the name gets licensed over and over again), and with it went all of the film for the camera that made it so useful. This new camera by Fuji brings back some of the fun of instant photos, though it is by no means perfect and it suffers from some of the same issues the older Polaroid camera had.

The idea is very straightforward - point-and-shoot, and the camera ejects an exposure that will develop over a few moments and will be fully developed in approximately 2 minutes. This is great for social events and is a fun way to share candid shots. The camera is very lightweight and it is small too so it is easy to pack and carry with you.

There are a few issues with the camera, though, some of which are very much like the old Polaroids of days gone by. The images do come out a bit grainy and are definitely not high resolution. If you are looking for images with nice, clean edge detail and bright, vibrant colors, this is going to disappoint you. Also, the images are really small, a little bigger than a passport picture but not by very much. And finally, the film is relatively expensive, a pack of exposures coming with only 10 slides and costing about $0.60 per exposure.

On the plus side, the camera is very easy to use and the camera body itself is not very expensive at all.

There are trade-offs with this camera. On one hand, it is super convenient, it’s fun and it’s relatively inexpensive. However, exposure quality is mediocre, pictures are small and on a per-picture basis the exposures are somewhat expensive. To me, the fun factor weighs heavily in favor of this camera and offsets some of the negatives. For social gatherings and recreational events, this is a fun camera and will serve well. Do not expect to have high-end results, though.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm Instax Mini 26 + Rainbow Film Bundle - Black

NETGEAR AC1200 Wi-Fi USB 3.0 Adapter for Desktop PC | Dual Band Wifi Stick for Wireless internet (A6210-100PAS) We have a router that supports the 802.11ac standard but until we got this router we had no way of connecting to it beyond the 802.11n standard. I was very interested in trying this adapter to see if it really is that much faster. It’s absolutely very fast and has wonderful connection reliability but suffers from a very slow software installation process.

I connected it to a Windows 7 64-bit system and allowed Windows to search for a driver. When that failed (as I assumed it would since this is a new product) I put in the installation CD and started the installer. The process took a surprisingly long time just to install and load the driver, to the point that I considered rebooting the box and starting over. It did finish though and then was ready to connect.

It connected without effort to our 5GHz network and immediately was able to serve up content. Everything seemed to be faster but we were not sure - until my teenage son connected to a Minecraft server and started playing. In addition to a lag-free connection he noticed about a 20% gain in frame rates sustained.

So far I can’t find anything beyond the clunky install that stands out as a negative. This is a fast adapter and it worth the one-time install time if you want fast, reliable connections and have a router that can handle the 802.11ac standard.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR AC1200 Wi-Fi USB 3.0 Adapter for Desktop PC | Dual Band Wifi Stick for Wireless internet (A6210-100PAS)

text_fidelity_a:
D-Link Day & Night Wi-Fi Camera with Remote Viewing (DCS-932L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) First of all, the D-Link camera is relatively easy to set up - always the one to play with techie stuff first, my husband had it up and running in a flash (well almost a flash). Just attach the supplied cable to your computer, run the CD and follow the simple instructions and you're good to go. According to the instructions, you have two options to set up the camera: wirelessly or wired. Naturally, my husband tried the wireless option first, which didn't work because it claimed (spuriously, we believe) that it couldn't find the network, so he had to resort to the other method, which worked right away. We're using a Linksys wireless router.

The camera works quite well indoors where the intensity of the ambient light is generally much lower than outdoors. However, in the brighter outdoor light it is difficult to discern what you're looking at (is it a bird, is it a plane?). The colour is not the best, but then again, it ain't a Nikon 7000. There is some amount of adjustment that can be done online to change the settings, but you'll need to create an online account/register your camera first with D-Link at [...] This is also necessary if you want to view your camera remotely. Strange enough, whenever I try to access the camera online, I get a message telling me that the application needs an earlier version of Java. However, after hitting <Run> for the next three dialogue boxes or so that pop up, it will display the picture. I tried accessing the camera from outside my home network but was unable to do so. Maybe firewall issues?? (Too much effort required to check this). There is also an iPod app that is quite good, minus sound.

Night vision was surprisingly good too. In the dark, the images were shades of grey, but in brighter conditions, the colour returned. Four LED lights lit up whenever the night vision was activated (could be an issue if you wanted to place it somewhere discrete).

On the down side, the camera has to be plugged into an electrical socket to work, and the cord it came with is very short. This means you have to either place it near an electrical outlet or use an extension cord. This would obviously have limitations on where you can place it. It also has to be connected to your home network whether wired or wireless.

While in theory it could be used as a security camera, it has to be powered 24/7, so if you live in a country or area prone to an uneven power supply which could damage sensitive equipment, then you may want to consider that before getting it or you may need to install additional equipment such as line conditioners/UPS to protect your equipment.

The sound is not very good. In fact, after a few hours use it started to make a clicking sound in an endless loop.

Recommended for limited applications such as keeping an eye on kids (or pets, or pesky guests), or when you're avoiding (hiding from) certain people who come calling at your gate, but not as a dedicated security system.

Amanda Richards, June 29, 2011
text_fidelity_b: D-Link Day & Night Wi-Fi Camera with Remote Viewing (DCS-932L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

adidas RPT-01 Bluetooth Sport On-Ear Headphones - Night Grey, 2.8 x 5.6 x 7.5 Inches I wear headphones when I work outside, spring through fall. By the end of fall, that year’s pair is pretty nasty from hours of daily use and me sweating in them. Of course I clean them, but it’s impossible to *really* deep clean headphones.

So that’s what drew me to the adidas RPT-01 Sport Headphones: the description advertises “removable, washable knitted ear cushions.” Knit covers I can wash? Hooray!

But there’s no instructions in the box on how to remove the ear covers or the headband. It turns out the cushions aren’t as removable as advertised.The ear cups twist off the headphones (a gentle, counter-clockwise turn), but there’s still an inner plastic rim. I thought I’d be able to wash the knitted cover itself, but nope. And I nearly tore the cover trying to figure out how to remove it, until I found the manual online.

I can’t figure out how to get the headband all the way off. The black plastic lining is removable, allowing the headband to be pushed up. I worry the headband will tear quickly, as the holes that line up with the black plastic lining aren’t reinforced.

Sound quality is okay … as long as I don’t use the Control Knob.

The Control Knob is like a volume rocker and skip/go back button in one. But when I used it to change the volume and skip tracks, I had static that lasted for several seconds.

There is an adidas Headphones app, but I thought it was useless. The only advantage of the app is that it allows you to set up to 3 customizable actions for the other button on the headphones. Oddly enough, at the time of writing this review, the app was only available on Android. I wanted to test the headphones on an iPhone too, but could not because the adidas Headphones app wasn’t available in my country (USA).

Lastly, the headphones are so uncomfortable to wear that I can’t wear them for more than 10 minutes. If I were inclined to use them, which I’m not, mainly because of the static whenever I use the Control Knob. I have a small head, but these headphones are tight and squeeze my ears and head. The ear cushions are actually quite scratchy too.
text_fidelity_b: adidas RPT-01 Bluetooth Sport On-Ear Headphones - Night Grey, 2.8 x 5.6 x 7.5 Inches

text_fidelity_a:
EVOO 14.1” Ultra Thin Laptop FHD, 32GB Storage, 4GB Memory, Micro HDMI, Front Camera, Windows 10 Home I honestly can’t think of an intended user for this laptop. It’s so sluggish that if I gave it to a kid, I can’t imagine them having the patience to wait for the *browser* to open. Let alone go to a website.

I’m a semi-patient adult in my 30s and wanted to chuck this laptop against the wall because the initial setup took so long. For an example, I tried to load the system information to find hardware information, and it took SEVEN seconds to open the Start Menu and load System Information.

The processor is an Intel(R) Celeron(R) CPU N3350 @ 1.10GHz. The laptop has 4GBs of RAM.

My three-year-old phone has 4GB of RAM and is snappier than the EVOO laptop. I have a Chromebook (Acer R11) that is also about three years old, and it’s snappier, too.

Windows 10 S is the default on the laptop, which doesn’t allow you to install any programs not from the Microsoft app store. I suppose that’s useful for basic users, but if you want to put another browser on, you have to disable S mode. Once you disable S mode, you can’t go back to it.

I thought I’d use this laptop for writing, since it’s so slow to load anything that I wouldn’t be tempted to go online. But I don’t even like typing on it; the keyboard feels like I’m typing on a cardboard box. There’s a hollow plastic sound when I type; it’s *that* flimsy. There are some keyboard shortcuts, but I thought it was odd that there wasn’t a shortcut to adjust the brightness. Considering how long it takes the Start Menu to load, that doesn’t make it easy to change the brightness of the screen.

The trackpad is decent, probably the best part of the laptop for me. It has a slightly sandy texture. For an inexpensive laptop, the trackpad isn’t bad.

The laptop is made in China.
text_fidelity_b: EVOO 14.1” Ultra Thin Laptop FHD, 32GB Storage, 4GB Memory, Micro HDMI, Front Camera, Windows 10 Home

Its slim profile. But it will still hold a lot of gear.

text_fidelity_a:
Stellar Labs,Outdoor FM Antenna OMNIDIRECTIONAL 9/12/2015
Final Review:
Have now completed the installation and hookup of this antenna. The first test was to listen to Mixed Bag, 90.7 FM which was always full of static. Now this station comes in crystal clear, loud, and strong. Note that I decided to mount this antenna on the side of my house, just beneath the peak of my low roof facing the back yard. I had a quantity of twin 300 ohm cable which I wanted to use. Using a 300ohm/75ohm converter, I simply attached the end of the cable to the two 300ohm screws, protecting the connection with electrical tape. I measured and fabricated a wood mounting plate (see photo) and then screwed the mast bracket to it from the back. The wooden support board was then lag screwed, in turn, to the outside of my house just below the peak using 5" long screws. I then installed the antenna and mast, after reversing it. It now extends upwards vertically yet does not interfere with the roof line. The versatility of the mast permitted me to accomplish that.

(This review is preliminary. I assembled the antenna but am not yet ready to install it.
Assembly tips:

- Both curved antenna segments are secured to the antenna cross bar with the supplied hardware.
- The ends of one (bottom) segment are held in place with two phillips head screws. First, remove the curved metal clamp. line up the holes in the segment and, maintaining hand pressure on each segment end to ensure that it is seated firmly into it's curved metal seat, insert each screw and secure. Do not over tighten these fasteners. This is the "bottom" of the antenna, opposite the 75 ohm connector side. Attach one leg of the segment at a time.
- The ends of the second (top) segment are held in place with two hex head nuts. You will note that each nut is topped with a rubber 'O' ring. This is used to keep the nuts from threading off until assembly. Do not attempt to re-use these as they are not spacers or washers.
- Again, seat the ends of the antenna segment firmly in place, aligning the holes over the studs. Holding down the segment, install each nut. Do not over tighten these nuts.
- The closed loop ends of each antenna segment may now be gently guided in front of the black plastic locking clips. Once the looped ends are in position, firmly, yet carefully snap them into place. The circular antenna shape has now been completed. If assembled patiently and slowly, damage should not occur to the antenna.)
text_fidelity_b: Stellar Labs,Outdoor FM Antenna OMNIDIRECTIONAL

text_fidelity_a:
BOSS Audio Systems B9351WRC Double Din, Touchscreen, Bluetooth, DVD CD MP3 USB SD AM FM Car Stereo, 6.2 Inch Digital LCD Monitor, Wireless Remote, Wireless Rear License Plate Camera. I knew, due to my disability, that I was going to need to find a professional installer to install this Boss Audio Systems B9351WRC head unit and wireless reverse camera along with two replacement door speakers I decided needed replacement (and wow, they really needed replacing). The installation took approximately three hours or so. The only problem which may not be a problem but I'm a worrier. The bracket for the wireless reverse camera somewhat, but not entirely, covers the plate expiration stickers somewhat. Other than that the head unit fit as good if not better than the stock radio fit. in the dashboard.
This radio plays AM/FM stations though there's very few decent radio stations around here. The unit also plays from USB thumb drives which plugs into a port under a panel under the volume/pause/power button. I put 600+ songs on a USB 2.0 16 GB driver and it played everything as far as I could tell. There might be a couple VBR or odd format MP3 files it may not play but I haven't gotten to them yes. Nothing's refused to play and even a couple that had imbedded album artwork actually showed up but so small it was almost impossible to see and I had no idea how to make it better. The instructions in the manual were basically "Play with things and see what happens!" more than specific directions how different functions work.
What I went with, is a 32 gig micro-SD card that had the same 600+ songs the thumb drive has. But with the micro-SD card you can close the hatch under the volume and control knob which you couldn't with the thumb drive. There's also an AUX input jack for old style MP3 players and phones.
The six inch screen is sharp and crisp. The backup camera, even with a streetlight thirty feet away had more than enough light to back out of my garage. I even backed down the street a ways in almost complete darkness and could see just fine with just the reverse lights on the car. Now as long as no cops have a problem with it I'm golden.
I tried home burned CDs and while it took a few seconds longer to recognize it played them fine. I tried store bought CDs and they played right off the bat. OH! and it plays DVD discs jut fine in case my passenger wants to watch a movie as we drive. I promise I'm no dumb enough to watch a movie while I drive.
According to the installer I can leave the micro SD card in the unit all the time. So, 600+ songs anytime I want which I can shuffle or randomly pick and play songs anytime I want. I couldn't be happier. With the stock deck I'd sometimes get to my destination just as the deck decided to recognize the CD so this deck is a godsend when I really needed a new one. Now with as many songs as I can cram into a 32 gig drive. Right now I've got 687 songs and tons of free space. I may have to start buying more music and ripping some more albums from my collection to add to my micro-SD card.
So I can play hundreds, thousands of MP3 songs on a micro-SD card. I can play CDs both homemade and store bought. I can watch DVDs on a pretty sharp (all settings can be changed in the system) the dimmer is a bit bright until it goes off completely but it's not too bad or too bright. There's a user setting EQ option as well as several other preset settings to choose from. There are options to add sound effects such as large hall, church, cavern, etc. I avoided them entirely and set my own EQ settings with the loudness off. The new speakers sound great for high end and midrange. The stock back speakers add some needed bass.
All in all? This is an affordable head unit with all the features and functions one could ask for. It comes with a remote that I'm not sure I'm even going to keep anywhere in the car. Anything you need to do can be done on the deck and no one's sitting in the back seat of a '07 Hyundai Accent, seriously. So the remote is useless but amusing.
I love this unit, the backup cam is awesome, The many ways to play music. The fit and finish, it's close to perfect.
This a little long and meandering review but I really like this radio and I'm glad I replaced the door speakers and went with a professional installer who's basically given me a lifetime warranty on his labor. I couldn't be happier.

Update 04-04-2017: It's been nearly six months since I had this head unit and backup camera installed. Radio reception is still bad, I still despise listening to radio so that's no big deal. Have kept a micro SD card loaded with hundreds of songs installed. Turn the unit on it automatically defaults to that. Everything is still working fine. Professional installation was worth the money.
text_fidelity_b: BOSS Audio Systems B9351WRC Double Din, Touchscreen, Bluetooth, DVD CD MP3 USB SD AM FM Car Stereo, 6.2 Inch Digital LCD Monitor, Wireless Remote, Wireless Rear License Plate Camera.

Koss 155524 UR40 Collapsible Over-Ear Headphones ...and after 13 years of heavy use, I was curious... here's my old headphones!

I went looking, because I like them so much all this time!

A couple things.

The mesh head thing- it only stayed on a couple years. They headphones worked better without it anyhow I think. Smoother on my hair. Which has a fine texture, and is a bit frizzy- lots of fine short pieces. Sometimes the foldable joints catch in them. This happens on earrings, necklaces, other headphones and other things as well. No more on this product really. Function of having fine curly hair.

Sound has always been fantastic. I love the sound and am sad when I send a ton of cash on headphones that don't come close.

They are not a snug fit, but, are soft enough and comfy enough to wear to bed. Because of the tender fabric, it's started to deteriorate on the smooth fake leathery bits. So so soft all this time though. Really to last 13 years, NO COMPLAINTS!!!.

Not snug enough to work out in. Snug enough to casually hike or walk in. They won't just fall right off or anything.

Lightweight. Easy to make a pouch or toss them into a ziplock freezer quart bag to travel and keep them in your pack or bag more tidily.

I would agree with most reviews. I tend to consider the cables 'supple' instead of 'flimsy'-- and this is an important difference! Supple cables don't just out at awkward angles and get caught on as much stuff. You can keep your music device in your pocket and the cable stays nicely under your coat or shirt and bends where you need it to stay and likes being there rather than tugging intself back in to the shape it wants to be in like a stiffer cable.

These are one of the few products I would give 10 stars to if I could.

And I still would after 13 years!!!!!!

Oh,

Actually they still work fine too. Really. I just noticed they are really a little fiddly nowadays because I used them so much, and was wondering if they still made them.

It's a bit disturbing that amazon remembered I bought them so long ago, though. I'm starting to hope Amazon never holds a grudge against me, cause they never forget!!
text_fidelity_b: Koss 155524 UR40 Collapsible Over-Ear Headphones

text_fidelity_a:
Blink Indoor Home Security Camera System with Motion Detection, HD Video, 2-Year Battery Life and Cloud Storage Included - 3 Camera Kit In terms of installation, it really doesn't get any easier: basically just plug in the control module and tap a couple buttons to register each camera and you're in business. Took me all of 5 minutes.

The cameras themselves aren't feature rich - you're not going to find tilt/swivel/zoom or even night vision. But you can't expect it from cameras that operate in 2 AA for up to 2 years! They do what they're designed to do: basic monitoring with motion detection in a completely wireless setup (you can literally place the cameras anywhere!). An LED light can illuminate any recording in darkness.

There's no monthly service fee either - but the recordings you can take are only up to a minute long and there's a limit on how many.

I love these cameras for their ease of setup and complete mobility. The only reason I'm not giving them 5 stars is the lack of an outdoor camera option and a little bit buggy iOS app.

Update (11/27/2017): a couple negatives to the cameras:
(1) while each camera comes with a wall mount, orienting it just right (in my case on a front porch so I could see who's at the door) isn't all that easy (just because the camera doesn't have an area in its view doesn't mean it won't detect motion slightly outside it!)
(2) the cameras have no speakers. I knew this when buying, of course, but competing cameras in same price range do.
(3) I just asked Blink whether there are any plans for Apple HomeKIt support - and there aren't :-( This is a big negative for me because I'm starting to do some home automation and since we're an Apple household, I want HomeKit. So I'm going to be looking for another set of cameras instead of expanding my Blink set :-(

All-New Fire HD 8 Screen Protector,Tempered Glass Screen Protector Film for All-New Fire HD 8 Tablet with Alexa (7th 2017 Release) [9H Hardness] [Crystal Clear] [Bubble Free] I've used glass screen protectors on several smartphones and digital cameras. This is my first time trying a large glass screen protector on a tablet. The kit contains everything you need, including a alcohol towel for cleaning your tablet (and your fingers), a sticker that tries to pick up all the lint on the tablet and the screen protector, and various other things that are less necessary. The glass is fine. It is slightly smaller than the Fire 8's screen (so you have some leeway if you don't install it perfectly). There is a little hole at the top so it doesn't cover the selfie camera. Honestly, I haven't noticed much difference between different brands of screen protectors.

If you've never installed a glass screen protector before, look on YouTube for tutorials. All of the similar products are installed the same way. You need to be really careful when installing this thing since it is large and difficult to align with your tablet's screen. I suggest that you try to align one edge of the protector as well as the camera hole and then hope for the best with the other edges. Make sure you pick up all the lint on both the tablet screen and the back of the screen protector, since any stray dust or lint is going to be noticeably ugly for as long as you have the screen protector installed. If you try to remove the screen protector to wipe off some lint that you missed, I guarantee that more lint will sucked in and make the problem worse, so you're best off doing a very thorough cleaning job the first time.

Whether or not you actually need a screen protector is a good question. If you use a case with a cover, then your chance of scratching the screen is small. I guess that depends on how rough you are with your tablet. You can go by your experience with other devices. A tablet is not like a smartphone that is sitting in your pocket with loose change and keys.
text_fidelity_b: All-New Fire HD 8 Screen Protector,Tempered Glass Screen Protector Film for All-New Fire HD 8 Tablet with Alexa (7th 2017 Release) [9H Hardness] [Crystal Clear] [Bubble Free]

Logitech for Creators Blue Yeti X Professional USB Condenser Microphone for PC, Mac,Gaming,Recording, Streaming, Podcasting on PC, Desktop Mic High-Res Metering, LED Lighting,Blue VO!CE Effects-Black This is a fancier version of the popular Blue Yeti amateur-quality USB microphone with a much higher price tag ($170 vs $110). For the extra money, you get 4 condensers (instead of 3) to give you higher-resolution 24-bit audio (instead of 16-bit) plus a bunch of fancier control and display options. The new microphone has the same directional recording patterns to isolate the recording to your intended audio sources. Is the new microphone worth the extra money? If you really need 24-bit audio, then definitely yes. If not, the new display and control features are more convenient than a huge jump in functionality. The Blue Yeti is still a great microphone for amateur USB recording (podcasts, musical performances, etc). The new version is a step forward, but not worth the price for everyone.

My biggest complaint is that the new microphone uses the same ancient mini-USB interface as the old one. Modern ultralight laptops are moving to the USB-C standard and mini-USB is 2 generations old. You could use a USB-C hub to give you a mini-USB interface, but I wish all modern devices came with USB-C ports since this has been the standard for the last few years.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech for Creators Blue Yeti X Professional USB Condenser Microphone for PC, Mac,Gaming,Recording, Streaming, Podcasting on PC, Desktop Mic High-Res Metering, LED Lighting,Blue VO!CE Effects-Black

I do appreciate the full integration of the Fire Stick with my other devices through our Amazon account - I can pick up a show on Prime with my tablet, phone or tv exactly where I left off. I have a few different hubs now because Apple decided I only needed USB-C ports on my laptop. Depending on what I’m doing and how many devices I need to plug in, I’ll either use a hub or adapters.

WiFi signal strength can be impacted by hubs or similar devices, there’s some interference with USB 3.0 and 2.4Ghz networks. It’s a known problem, there’s a lot about it online if you’ve also run into it. I’ve noticed this using other hubs, and I have about the same degree of interference with this one.

I don’t love the design of this hub. I wish the hub’s USB-C plug was straight, not an “L.” While I can still plug in other USB-C things next to the hub, the “L” shape of the plug dictates how the hub sits on my desk.

The hub is bigger than it needs to be. Maybe if the glassy front was repurposed, the USB 3.0 ports laid out in a square rather than a line, it wouldn’t take up as much room on my desk. The big display only has a tiny icon to show me when the hub is on … I just don’t like the wasted space.
text_fidelity_b: Baseus USB-C Docking Station, USB C Data Hub Adapter with PD Type C Charging Port, 5-in-1 USB C Dongle Adapter for MacBook/Pro/Air 2018,Chromebook,XPS,Galaxy S10/S9/S8/Note9

text_fidelity_a:
Monoprice Blackbird 4K 3x1 HDMI 1.4 Switch - Compact, HDCP 2.2, Built-in Equalizer, 4K 30Hz, YCbCr 4:4:4, 18Gbps (Compatible with PS4/5 Xbox Apple TV Fire Stick Roku Blu-Ray Player) Since we mounted our TV we like to use as few chords as possible. This way they are neatly tucked along the wall and down into the entertainment center where all our entertainment equipment is housed. So the main HDMI cable runs down but of course we have more components that require a cable than the one connected to the TV. Our solution? A signal splitter. Thankfully, we have only three output connections so this one seemed perfect. Plus, it touts 4k signal, even though most pre-4k HDMI boxes should be fine, but it's nice to have that in the title just in case.

What I use this mostly for is the cable box and a couple of video game systems. As for the cable box, seems to work fine; no dropped signals that I've noticed, nor any degradation in quality. As for game consoles, I have the PS3 and the Wii U hooked up to it. SAme: no noticeable quality degradation nor input lag.
Now, to put it to the real test, I hooked up some retro consoles that have been modded to output native HDMI; that means they'll be HDMI with no lag. Considering I have this and two HDMI cables connecting the console to the TV, I was curious to see if there truly was any lag.
With older games, timing is everything, especially on the 8-bit consoles with platformers and fighters, like the NES. From what I could tell, there was absolutely no lag, not to mention signal loss. The buttons responded as though I were using a normal NES on a CRT.

So yeah, I'm pretty satisfied. It's a bit light and doesn't have heavy pads on the bottom to prevent it from sliding around. With so many cables, and the ability to use the remote control, it should be a bit more stable on the surface.
I haven't used the remote as the detections are instant. No need to manually switch the inputs, at least from my experience. Also, I didn't need to use the power adapter; the power from the HDMI cables seemed to be sufficient, and the detection was not complicated by the lack of adapter. Weird.
text_fidelity_b: Monoprice Blackbird 4K 3x1 HDMI 1.4 Switch - Compact, HDCP 2.2, Built-in Equalizer, 4K 30Hz, YCbCr 4:4:4, 18Gbps (Compatible with PS4/5 Xbox Apple TV Fire Stick Roku Blu-Ray Player)

Mohu Leaf 50 Amplified Indoor TV Antenna, 60-Mile Range, UHF/VHF Multi-directional, Paper-Thin, 16 ft. Coaxial Cable, 15dB Amplifier with USB Cable, Reversibile, Paintable, 4K-Ready HDTV, MH-110584 After a bad experience with another flat amp antenna I purchased the leaf for just over $50 .
It picks up 19 stations in the "low country" around a lot of tall pine trees.(20 is the max number of stations in a 60 mile radius here with any antenna according to the TV manufacturer).

You can paint the ant/ cables to match the walls. Comes with push pins for walls and Velcro for wall or window if you want them.Also has a plug into TV for the amp or you can plug into the wall like I did so it isn't hampered by the surge protector.

I get ABC, CBS,NBC,FOX,THIS,3 PBS stations, 3 Christian channels,a Spanish channel, WE,GET,MY,BOUNCE,YOU TOO, one music video channel and one other. The reception on all (but 2) is exceptionally strong with no blips in power even if you cannot put it in a window. I have mine hanging behind my curtain and most channels get 90-100% station strength almost constantly when 35%, even 30% will give you the station clear enough to watch a program with very few "blips" in reception.

I am enjoying not adjusting the Rabbit ear antenna (when I watched certain channels) even though it worked *good* enough for the money.

If you had another antenna before that only picked up 5-13 channels (for exp.) and you switch to a more powerful one like this, remember to unplug your TV a good minute before re- auto programming ( I forgot at first myself) as some TVs seem to "remember" how many it gets and stops at that number.

No need for an ugly outside antenna with this one.

When I use my hair dryer or turn on another "power draw", it doesnt get the interference the previous amplified antenna had, so probably uses less electricity, yet pulls in more stations.
I'm very happy with it. I get more channels than my basic cable had that I enjoy watching also.
text_fidelity_b: Mohu Leaf 50 Amplified Indoor TV Antenna, 60-Mile Range, UHF/VHF Multi-directional, Paper-Thin, 16 ft. Coaxial Cable, 15dB Amplifier with USB Cable, Reversibile, Paintable, 4K-Ready HDTV, MH-110584

But there are a few items that don't fit that profile: my electric toothbrush for instance. For some years I've been carrying a clunky voltage converter, but this power strip style really is more convenient: you can plug in several items, and also use the USB ports to charge the phone/tablet/Kindle trio that seems to be a must-have for most of us. The power cable for this item has a Euro plug, so you need an adapter for non-Euro countries including the US. They provide several of them (see product description): US, UK, Australia, Italy, Israel. (Note however that they erroneously say the UK plug works in India: it doesn't, you need to get yourself a separate one for that part of the world.)

I'm not travelling yet, so can't confirm that it does work for step-down operation in 220-240v countries. I've tested it here, and it works just fine. The USB charging ports are particularly satisfactory, they clearly put out the advertised power for fast charging.

Overall an excellent and very useful product.

X-mini Liberty True Wireless Earbuds Bluetooth 5.0 in-Ear Stereo Earphones Built-in Dual Mic, 14H Playtime, Sports Earphones for Running Gym Workout, Dynamic Driver, One Step Pairing, 1 Year Warranty These jumped out at me because of the case design so I was really looking forward to trying them. Unfortunately, the case is where the excitement ended. Pairing is simple, just pull them out of the case. You can use these together or just one at a time. These are really small but they actually stayed in my ears and that’s also while I slept. They are also pretty comfortable. The battery life is awful. They had a straight playtime at 3 hours and 20 minutes. I need the battery to last at least 9 hours and that’s really not difficult to do. I have a few earbuds that last 3 times that and at half the price. Next would be the sound quality and that was also an epic fail. If the volume would have gone past the highest aloud the bass would have been a bit better. If you need to make or receive any calls, these will definitely not work. text_fidelity_a:
Philips DVT5000/00 4 GB Digital Voice Tracer with 3 Built-in Microphones Voice Recorder This is a good voice recorder. Whether you need it to record your voice memos, lectures, meetings, or discretely record your favorite spy, this will surely be a recorder you'll find many uses for.

It feels very secure in your hand, and has a comfortable feel and weight. It comes with a small pouch, which is nice. The record button is easy to find my sight or feel. The volume and forward/reverse buttons are on an outer button from the record button. Play and stop on the left and index and menu are on the right.

f1 and f2 buttons are primarily used for setting mic sensitivity and voice quality. Under Mic Sensitivity you can choose: Dictate (good for personal memos), Speech recognition (turns on when it hears voice), conversation (good for interviews or conversations, auto zoom (good for large areas where there may be close up voices and far voices), and lecture (good for lectures)

You can choose either low quality at 8kbps in Mp3 format to super high quality 192kbps in mp3. There is also a wave format in 1411 kbps. The higher quality you go impacts total record time. You can add a micro SD card for adding recording time.

There are also 4 index folders labeled A thru D. These are for separating projects. There is also a folder you could place music files if you wanted this to be a mp3 player.

There is also a menu setting where the voice quality and mic sensitivity can be accessed as well as numerous other options such as splitting files, display contrast, and clearvoice (an option that improves the sound quality of the recorded voiec)

The unit comes with rechargable AA batteries that will need to be charged when you first open it. They charge with the included usb to micro USB cord. Any other micro USB cord you own will also work. Once the recorder is connected to your computer through the USB cable you can download and upload voice or mp3 and wave files.

The only thing I wish this had was different settings for each index. For instance I would have liked to set index A for lecture mode at high quality, index B for dictate at a lower quality, etc. Once you set a mic sensitivity and recording quality, they are the same for all index until you change them in settings.

Overall a great quality recorder. Great for meetings, memos, and conversations.
text_fidelity_b: Philips DVT5000/00 4 GB Digital Voice Tracer with 3 Built-in Microphones Voice Recorder

text_fidelity_a:
Display Port to HDMI Converter with Audio Adapter I wanted to hear and see Skype on our Sony XBR7 HDMI-only capable 1080p TV, fed from a Lenovo X220 convertable laptop/tablet running System 7 64 bit Ultimate through the DisplayPort. I also wanted to watch some YouTube videos playing from Firefox and hear their audio on my big living room audio system. No such luck.

When first plugged in, I remember briefly seeing the TV via this DisplayPort adapter in the audio device list, but the next time, the TV disappeared and is nowhere to be found. Not in the audio control panel, anyway. It's just gone.

I first chalked this up to the Thinkpad weirdness, as its internal audio card/mic doesn't work with Skype either. If I plug in an external Logitech webcam, it works seamlessly. Internal camera/mic, nothing.

Sony audio problems aside, the video looks great on the big screen, though it overscans a bit and cuts off part of the menu bar at the bottom.

One reviewer said he could see his TV in the list of audio devices and was able to configure its audio to satisfaction. My Sony TV does not show in the Lenovo audio devices list, though it does show as a generic PnP monitor.

I plugged the HDMI cable into a tiny 7" video monitor and whatdayaknow, the audio came through and the device showed up as an audio device. Then I plugged it into a 20" Vizio and sure enough, it works fine too. Same with a Samsung LCD. Three monitors out of four work. The Sony is the only one that doesn't. Hmmmm.

Sooooo, I'm guessing there's something about Sony's DRM or some other HDMI protocol blocking the computer from seeing the TV. I set all the TVs for internal speakers. Routing audio to an external amp is another variable in the equation.

Nothing wrong with the adapter that I can tell, it simply doesn't see certain Sony TV's.
text_fidelity_b: Display Port to HDMI Converter with Audio Adapter

We got another one listed at $40 and besides for the branding, it seems to be the same binocular with slight molding differences. The tech is the same. Don't bother spending a little more unless you really want to upgrade and get one with zoom function. All these economy versions do not have zoom. And if you're new to binoculars, there is a learning curve, but this is how you focus:

1. Set the RIGHT EYEPIECE dial to ZERO and set sight on a distant subject. I'm not sure what zero means since there are no numbers, but there are arrows, so I presume it's when the arrows line up.

2. Cover the RIGHT FRONT lens with your hand, and rotate the FOCUSING WHEEL (the middle wheel), until the image is sharp. Keep both eyes open while you make this adjustment.

3. Now cover the LEFT FRONT lens and rotate the RIGHT EYEPIECE dial until the image is sharp. So here, you're not touching the focusing wheel, you're adjusting the RIGHT EYEPIECE dial.

text_fidelity_a:
SK hynix Gold S31 1TB SATA Gen3 2.5 inch Internal SSD | SSD 1TB | Up to 560MB/S | Solid State Drive | Compact 2.5" SSD Form Factor SSD | Internal Solid State Drive | SATA SSD Revving up old Macs is like one of my favorite things. I don't do much of it anymore, because (a) arthritis in my hands has made the turning of tiny screws much more of a chore, and (b) I was running out of old Macs.

The last one I had was a 2010 mini that was the first computer I'd bought new since probably 1993 (also a Mac). It had the last of the Core2Duo processors and a spin up hard drive and a couple of gigs of ram that I upgraded pretty much right away. It served as a DVR for a while, then a minecraft server, media streamer, then got put away. I resurrected it to bounce DATS to .WAV to mp3 when I learned that it had digital audio input and output. I had been researching all these expensive things to make that happen, and it turned out that my little friend was able to save me hundreds of dollars with something that had been built in all along.

But it was slow because of the HDD. And upgrading looked really daunting. I'd done one of the earlier minis, and it had been an exercise in anxiety.

But the other day, I decided to give it a try. Two bits of advice: if you can get through this without disconnecting the wifi connector (you can if you are really careful), do so, and (2) if you accidentally disconnect the wifi connector (I did), don't panic. Watch videos of people putting iPhones back together (the older, the better). These connectors are fussy. Do not force them. If they are seated correctly, a light press will connect them. You'll feel the click. But it's almost like threading a needle to get it seated correctly. And if you push too hard, you'll break it. Same with the fan. Just be careful. If you are pushing and it's not connecting right away, it's not lined up right.

Okay, so deciding to do the drive replacement took awhile because the above two steps seemed very daunting. And the project took me several hours, because I had to stop and rest a few times (if your hands work and you keep your screws organized, it should take about 45 minutes). But it was worth every minute.

This is an excellent drive. The form factor lines up exactly with the HDD I pulled from the mini (some of the drives I have used in old white MacBooks and older MacBook Pros have not). Not a millimeter off. The OS install flew. This drive is stellar in this context. If you need a 2.5" SSD, I highly recommend this one.
text_fidelity_b: SK hynix Gold S31 1TB SATA Gen3 2.5 inch Internal SSD | SSD 1TB | Up to 560MB/S | Solid State Drive | Compact 2.5" SSD Form Factor SSD | Internal Solid State Drive | SATA SSD

text_fidelity_a:
NYNE Multimedia Inc Cruiser Portable Bluetooth Speaker (Grey/Green) Although there are a lot of positive points to be said about this product, a major flaw with it is that - even on low volumes and on songs without much bass - you can hear a bit of distortion, like crackly static, that sounds like a speaker that you're either working too hard or is at the end of its life. This becomes worse as the battery gets low. I consider this issue to be "understandable and sort of acceptable" considering the whole system has to run on battery power and most people aren't expecting high power out of such a setup. They might just have a high-pass crossover set too high to conserve power, and too much is cut off, resulting in messy sound.

When you charge your phone with the speaker's battery (which in itself is sort of a nice, if cannibalistic, feature, one that other devices claim even though it is inherent to the device; with this, the USB-A port was added specifically for this purpose), it lowers the volume to level 8 (there is nothing to tell you what level you're at) to keep from draining the battery quickly. Even at this medium level and below, this problem can be recognized.

The bike mounts are 4" apart, center to center, so make sure you have room on your bike handlebars if that is your purpose for ordering. Included bike mounts are good. It also comes with a neoprene case, a USB cable, and an audio cable, both red. With all these extras trying to give the appearance of premium, it doesn't actually come with a charger, not that this will be an issue for most people (you probably already have more than you know what to do with).

There should be keyhole slots built into the bike mounts so it could also be hung on the wall and removed easily, making it more versatile.

The unit pairs easily and immediately with my Blackberry every time, and it can control the tracks through the BT connection as well. It looks well made and has a good feel to it. It looks like it could almost be waterproof, although I noticed no mention or claim of that feature (so I'm sure it's not).

The sound overall isn't bad for a low voltage battery operated speaker, as long as you're not sitting down and listening too closely. I guess for the purposes of making noise as you ride around the neighborhood, it'll do just fine.
text_fidelity_b: NYNE Multimedia Inc Cruiser Portable Bluetooth Speaker (Grey/Green)

Wacom Bamboo Splash Pen Tablet (CTL471) Just a few days ago I finally decided it was time to give my old Genius 8x6 MousePen up. It was time to upgrade to a Wacom. I browsed for a day or two trying to decide what would best suit me, and after a lot of thought I decided this would be the tablet I purchased. It arrived the earliest day it said it would arrive, and that was a treat.

After I opened it up I thought this tablet would be too small since my other one was a bit bigger, but I tested it out in one of the programs that came with it, ArtRage Studio, and was very surprised. I barely realized the drawing space was small, and it was very comfortable and felt very natural to be drawing on. The tablet itself does not take up much space at all, and it's very light and small enough to be easy to work around. ArtRage Studio is also a very nice bonus. It's a great alternative to Photoshop and other programs (I actually see myself using this program more than my Photoshop). The Splash also came with three spare pen nibs for when your current one wears down.

The pen is also very nice in that it doesn't use batteries, and it also fits comfortably in your hand.

I am a little disappointed that this isn't compatible with a wireless connection, but the cord on the tablet really isn't that obtrusive.

I'm very happy with my very first Wacom product, and I hope I can upgrade once more in a few years.

text_fidelity_a:
Antennas Direct DB2 Multi Directional HDTV Antenna (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I recently purchase an Antenna's Direct Clearstream 4 to use in my attic to feed the TVs in the BR and LR. Works fantastic, so when I needed another antenna for a TV in the study that I could not hook up to the antenna in the attic, I again went with Antenna's Direct, but this time picked the DB2 since it was smaller (and cheaper).

Absolutely fantastic reception! The only station it does not pull in as well as the Clearstream 4 was one fringe station. As with the Clearstream 4 positioning is a breeze - I just propped it up in the corner!

Given how well it performs, I thought I'd see how it does in the attic in place of the much larger and more expensive Clearstream. It does nearly as well - all the major networks come in equally good, and the DB2 picks up all but one of the more distant stations. The one it misses is a channel I never watch anyway, so for me, the two are equal.

For me (located outside Wash DC) the antennas pull in 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, 5, 7.1, 7.2, 7.3, 9.1, 9.2, 14.1, 20.1, and about a dozen PBS stations rock solid. Channels 66.1 to 66.4 are so-so on the DB2 and pretty good on the Clearstream 4.

The Clearstream 4 also pulls in several analog stations. I didn't try that with the DB2 so I don't know if it will work with analog. Come February, the point will be moot anyway, so I didn't bother to test it out for analog.

So, if you're debating between the Clearstream 4 and the DB2 (or DB4), give the DB2 a shot first - the little guy may do the trick, and you can save quite a bit of cash.
text_fidelity_b: Antennas Direct DB2 Multi Directional HDTV Antenna (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Sunon Desk Computer Monitor Stand Riser 2-Tier Wood Desktop Stand Riser for Printer Monitor Laptop TV (16.7 Inch-Dark Walnut) I needed this stand for something a little bit different than what it is for. I needed to have this for my essential oil cases. I have two of them with drawers and a wood panel that shuts over them when not in use. I was moving them to a top of a bookcase, but still needed a place for a phone book, or other small items. This case was PERFECT. Let's take a look.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This case comes in parts. There are pre-cut particle board covered with a vinyl type wood grain. I have the dark wood color. The pieces are well marked and there is plenty of cushioning in the box to help it not get scratched or broken up. There is also a bag of metal components.

HOW ARE THE INSTRUCTIONS?
The instructions for this stand are great. Everything is VERY well marked, very well laid out and if you are a visual learner, this will work beautifully for you. Everything is well illustrated too.

HOW DOES THIS GO TOGETHER?
I have to say that this went together quickly and easily. I was amazed at how fast it did go together.

IS IT STURDY?
This is plenty sturdy to hold my two cases of essential oils.

ANY PROBLEMS?
The only issue I had with this is that the screw caps that have to tighten around the metal posts to hold this together have to be turned. The problem is that the shelf is very narrow and it was hard to get my hand in there. It took some doing, but it eventually worked.

DOES THE TOOL COME WITH THIS?
Yes, this comes with a philips head allen key wrench.

QUALITY?
The edges of this show that the covering is not on perfectly. It is not going to be a flawless job, but once put together, it looks fine.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Whether for a monitor or another function like I chose with my essential oil cases, this stand is nice. It is compact, yet has space for thin books, workbooks or packs of papers- only thin ones though.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. The instructions and included tool pushed this up to five stars. I am IMPRESSED with how they went out of their way to be sure it went together well and easily.

Paying a bit extra for no ads was worth it, and I enjoy the drawings that serve as screensavers. When I'm reading a book, it automatically opens to the page I left off on just like my old kindle.

I only vaguely miss having the 3G function my old kindle had because I used to live out in the boonies with limited internet access. However, the WiFi has been generally sufficient and now I just make sure I download a few books before I travel.

Overall, the kindle has definitely revolutionized the way I read since it first came out when I was in high school. I do still keep a lot of hard copies of my favorite series and enjoy reading real books from time to time, but the kindle is SO easy to download anything, anytime you want. Not to mention bringing a whole library with you in one slim package while traveling! I have had this model for a year and a half now, and have no issues or complaints at this time.

text_fidelity_a:
co2CREA Hard Case with Sleep Mode Replacement for Apple AirPods Max Headphone (Black Case + Inside Red) First, mine didn’t smell.

Now that I have the positive attributes out of the way let’s discuss why you should avoid this case.
I reluctantly paid $33 for this and I have to wonder what I was thinking. It’s nowhere near worth that much.

It will not/cannot survive a side impact. Well that’s not true. It cannot protect your APM from a hit or drop that could damage them from the top. I’m not sure if it could from the bottom or sides. It’s either molded cardboard or thin plastic covered with fabric. No padding, just fabric.

Internally there is another layer of cardboard (or plastic, thin, very thin) covered in a felt like material. There’s absolutely no drop protection.

The magnets designed to put the APM into “sleep” mode lay flat. You will have to pinch them up while putting your headphones into it if you wish to keep them from clanging together and not using the stock case. Even then the magnets don’t work every time. See my pic.

Overall this is a $10 case marked up cause they can. I mean we have expensive headphones so why not charge us more? We have already proven we will pay.

Skip this thing. Mine is going back. If you want something to protect them in a backpack then still look elsewhere. You can get something equal to this for less.

Thanks for your time.

text_fidelity_a:
Sony BDP-BX370 Blu-ray Disc Player with built-in Wi-Fi and HDMI cable UPDATE 05/15/2021 - It lasted less than two weeks and it died. During playback the player freezes on discs known to be good, and in order to get6 the player to respond I have to disconnect the power from it. It was great while it lasted, I guess.

Original review follows.

===

I have wanted a Blu-Ray player for a while and I have had reason to suspect that my DVD player is dying. I have a flat-screen Sony television so I figured this player would connect and work with it without too much effort. I was right and it has worked very well for my family and me.

This is a straightforward device. I connected it to the TV via the provided HDMI cable, selected that input and immediately was able to get signal from it. I popped in a disc and it loaded up to the menu. That’s exactly what I expected to happen. In operation using the remote it has worked very much like my old DVD player – remote is laid out a bit differently but the operation is the same and it provides buttons to stop, fast forward and reverse, pause, eject, select the root menu and more. The remote had given us no issues so far, though it does need to have near line-of-site with the player in order for the player to see it and respond.

The footprint is much smaller than my older DVD player and required a bit of rearrangement in my entertainment center. The whole unit is smaller than a ream of paper and weighs next to nothing.

It has built-in WiFi and makes it easy to access online streaming services. However, I will confess that I haven’t yet tried this as I try to keep my WiFi device list small. I will experiment with this when there is time.

So far we have seen no issues with playback – no skips or stutters or freezes. I have a couple of discs that I know to cause issues for my DVD player that I will try in this player and see if it fares better, though I believe the discs are actually bad.

So far I have had a positive experience with this player and based on that I am happy to recommend it. It seems to work well and it is easy to understand and operate. It isn’t particularly expensive either which is a big plus.
text_fidelity_b: Sony BDP-BX370 Blu-ray Disc Player with built-in Wi-Fi and HDMI cable
