DeLUX Rechargeable Ergonomic Wireless Mouse Silent, 1600DPI, Reduce Hand and Wrist Pain, Vertical Mouse with USB Receiver and BT 5.0, 6 Buttons and Removable Palm Rest (M618G DB-Black) Update:

After 4 months I still have not found a hand position I like. What I settled on 'works' but I can't reach the forward a page button and my thumb just reached the page back button. On the good side, it charges fine and holds a charge for a long time. It takes a little time to get used to having to single click to wake the mouse but to me, it's no big deal.

For people looking for help with mouse/tennis elbow it definitely helped with that.

Original review:

The wheel is by far my biggest issue with this mouse.

I like some resistance, and feeling some click as I scroll but this is too much. Also, the wheel is way too stiff to click without moving the mouse and the wheel feels too far back to use my middle finger. I'm going to have to learn to scroll with my index finger and see how that works.

The primary buttons left and right-click feel pretty good, a little bit of resistance, but feel just about right to me but the position of them does not feel 'right'. My hand can't 'decide' if my ring finger wants to rest there or my middle finger. Neither feels right. With my middle finger on the right-click button, it feels too far apart. With my ring finger, then the right-click button feels too close.

The forward button (the top button) is very hard to click without pressing the left-click button.
Overall the shape is comfortable and I have no problem with my hand slipping or hitting the foward-back accidentally.

My hand-measured as a medium-sized hand but this feels just a little big to me. If you are on the low side of medium maybe go down a size.

I use this on my bed and it does not slide as well as the two Logitech mice I use even though both of those mice are heavier. It works it just does slide as easily and I will just have to get used to it. If I'm drawing I will need to get out one of my traditional mice.

Overall, it feels cheap.

I bought this to help with mouse/tennis elbow and I think it will help with that from how it feels to hold.

I'll spend some time with it, but at this point, I think it's going to go back because of the position and feel of the wheel and the 'odd' feeling position of the buttons.
text_fidelity_b: DeLUX Rechargeable Ergonomic Wireless Mouse Silent, 1600DPI, Reduce Hand and Wrist Pain, Vertical Mouse with USB Receiver and BT 5.0, 6 Buttons and Removable Palm Rest (M618G DB-Black)

Amazon Basics Standby UPS 600VA 360W Surge Protector Battery Power Backup - 8 Outlets, Black I'm pleased with the performance and features of this UPS. While it does not have the features that my other UPS's have (such as a screen that displays battery status, load, etc.) that's a plus, since I don't often use, or need, the info on the screen. This has just a simple on/off button, a mute button, and basic LED indicators that show if it's on line power or battery power.

It comes with the battery leads detached. Before use you need to remove the battery access panel (very simple -- just two screws) and connect the battery (also a very simple process).

I use it to for my router and cable modem so I can maintain Internet access and wifi during a power outage. I've simulated a power outage and both the modem and router didn't skip a beat. While this has a smaller capacity than the UPS's I use for my PCs, the 1000VA 550W specs are more than adequate to maintain a long run time given the light load.

One quibble -- and I have the same one with most UPS systems -- is that the outlets are too closely spaced, making it difficult to use all of them when plugging in devices that have a wall wart at the end. I would also have liked to see the outlets be color coded so you can more easily tell the difference between the bank of outlets that are surge protected only, and the bank that is surge/battery protected.

Those quibbles aside, it's been a good performer that provides all the features needed at a decent price.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics Standby UPS 600VA 360W Surge Protector Battery Power Backup - 8 Outlets, Black

Build quality of this one is good and weighs in at 28.3 ounces. They include an exposed extension cord that is too short. You will need to roll up your sleeves and get to work if you don't have an outlet near the location you want to put these lights. Or, if you want to go the easy route, then simply buy a longer exposed extension cord. Otherwise, you'll need to splice and dice! Recently, I installed a wifi extender in the garage, which is the only reason why I got these floodlights, otherwise, I would not have bothered getting these lights. text_fidelity_a:
TP-Link AC750 Wireless Wi-Fi Gigabit Router (Archer C2) I am not super "techie" like some of the other folks reviewing this router, just your average housewife who likes gadgets and tries not to drown in the constant wave of weekly tech improvements. As such, I wanted a new router to replace our two year old dual band Belkin with similar speed output, but only a single antenna. The Belkin had a number of dead spots despite using one of those extender things and I had had enough. Enter this TP-Link router.

I was wary of the installation after seeing some other reviews and the difficulties folks have been reporting. However, after reading the box and the instructions fully FIRST and then following the directions exactly, I had no problems. One thing I did notice immediately, is this router is meant to be used with a cable modem and that modem must be powered off before you connect it to this router. I used the website installation method and was up and going in a total of 20 minutes - that is from opening the box to having all our wireless stuff connected to the internet again. The website management page is very detailed and allows for a lot of customization of your network, honestly, more than I need or understand. But changing the router's password and setting our network name was simple and worked on the first try.

After three days of use I like it. The speed is decent and the dual antenna set up has improved the coverage problem we were having with the old Belkin router. I haven't experienced any slowdown or degradation of connectivity with multiple devices going at once thus far. A Fire Phone surfing the net, Fire tablet streaming music, laptop doing email, and a smart tv streaming video all at once in different rooms. So...a good router for every day family use in a pretty typical home.

*********** UPDATE FEBRUARY 2015 ***********
After 90 days this router is trouble free and really working like a champ. Our cable company upgraded our modem and increased our internet speeds recently, requiring a full shutdown and reconnect of my entire network. It was a snap and the router has had no problem with faster connection and the new modem. I relocated everything to the center of our house when everything was being swapped out and the router is now sending a five bar signal out to the back deck, which means I can sit out there with the dogs in nice weather to do email etc.

*****************UPDATE APRIL 2016 *************

I'm still using this router every single day for literally every single WiFi device in our house and it just does its job with zero drama every day. We now have two tablets, two smartphones, three DVR boxes on WiFi, two laptops, a printer, a Fire Stick for streaming movies, a smart tv connected the web now and then, and the Echo that's connected all the time. (yeah, I know...we watch a LOT of television in this house!)

Right this minute I am streaming music on the Echo, recording tv shows on two different DVR boxes, using my laptop to update this review, and uploading 42 photos from my phone to the cloud and pushing email to my tablet. Oh - and I am sitting outside on the patio enjoying the lovely spring day. This router is powerful and I have no dead spots inside or out in the backyard.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link AC750 Wireless Wi-Fi Gigabit Router (Archer C2)

Canon EF 24-105mm f/4 L IS USM Lens for Canon EOS SLR Cameras The Canon 24-105mm f/4 L lens with Image Stabilization is a fantastic lens for those times when you just want to have one lens on the camera but you also want to have a lot of options with your focal range. The range on this lens takes you from a decent wide angle perspective to a mid-range telephoto without any light loss (the maximum aperture is constant throughout the zoom range) and image stabilization keeps focus problems due to hand shake well away.

Optical quality is excellent, as you would expect with an L lens, and autofocus is smooth and fast. text_fidelity_a:
1MORE iBFree In-Ear Earphones Wireless Headphones with Bluetooth 4.2 AAC, IPX 6 Waterproof, Secure Fit, In-Line Mic for Sports Gym Running - New Model Black We blow through ear buds in our house and it seems that everyone has different ones that they like and don't like. Let's see how these measure up:

WHAT ARE THESE EAR BUDS LIKE?
These ear buds come in a nice box with a little instruction booklet. There is a little bag with three sets of gel caps in it. There are also three sets of hooks. Each of them comes in small medium and large. The hooks keep the buds in the ear but are soft so they don't hurt the ear at all.

The controls are on the right ear- the top hits about where the chin is. The connecting cord is big enough to be worn in front or back. The set comes with a cord but you have to have your own USB access to plug it into whether it be on an outlet or computer.

COMFORT
One of the most comfortable and secure earbud/headsets we have used to date- love that the hooks that help hold them in are soft so they don't hurt the ear, even after worn for a while.

PERFORMANCE
VOLUME
The headset gets the best result for us with the volume on max on the headset and halfway on the tablet that we use it with.

HIGHS/LOWS/MIDS
One of the things with this headset is that the highs are really nice and strong and so are the lows. The problem seems to be that the mids are drowned out making it feel like it is a bit out of balance. We have messed with it quite a bit and it seems to be the way it is.

SOUND PROOFING
These have excellent sound insulation capabilities. That does mean, however, that you need to be careful where you are wearing them if you need to hear what is around you or not.

BATTERY ALERT
When you first turn on the headphones, it will identify itself, tell you it is pairing and then give you an idea of how much battery life you have left- low, medium, or high.

POWER BUTTON
The power button is nice. Volume/skip functions are a challenge to get used to as compared to other Bluetooth headsets. There are sequences and timing as compared to others which seem to be simpler to use.

PAIRING
Very good pairing on all of the different devices we tested this with- several phones from Moto G3, Blu phone, Samsung Tablets and our stereo (forgot brand)

CHARGE
A charge has been lasting a good six to eight hours for us. Recharging seems to take us about three hours.

THE BOTTOM LINE
These are comfortable headphones that are easy to use, stay in the ears well, and have good insulation from ambient noise in the room or surroundings. They have nice highs and lows but tend to drown out the mids. The controls are a bit more challenging to learn at first as compared to other Bluetooth head sets we have used.

MY RATING
FOUR AND A HALF STARS- not able to give that so I am doing four. It is more like four and a half. The sound could be a little more balanced, and the controls not quite so difficult, but this is still a great set of headphones and we like it a lot.
text_fidelity_b: 1MORE iBFree In-Ear Earphones Wireless Headphones with Bluetooth 4.2 AAC, IPX 6 Waterproof, Secure Fit, In-Line Mic for Sports Gym Running - New Model Black

Case Logic TBC-411 DSLR Compact Backpack (Black) There’s some good points to this bag, but there are also a number of limitations that keep it at a three star rating.

On the plus side, the build quality is, in usual Case Logic fashion, well done. Strong, even stitching throughout; nice straps and buckles; good quality zippers with easy to find pull tabs. It feels and looks quite nice.

Unfortunately, the overall design does not meet as high of a standard. The padding is thin throughout. While I know this is for lighter, smaller DSLRs, I did not feel it provided much security for my Canon Rebel XT with just a couple of lens (50mm and 85mm). It’s not a size issue – just to see if I could, I was able to fit in my Canon 5D Mark II with the Canon 70-200L zoom plus the hood. It’s not a size issue, but rather a padding issue. The foam is thin and is not nearly as dense and bump absorbing as packs from Tenba, Lowepro or Crumpler. Granted, this is addressing a lower price point, but it’s not that low. Other lower-end bags I’ve tried have far more robust padding.

The slot for the tablet is another issue. Great idea; poor execution. There is very little padding for the tablet – forget about putting in a tablet unless it has a hard case, since this backpack won’t offer much protection. Same for the side pockets which have no padding.

This is a good choice if you’re looking to tote very little gear and are willing to bring along the cases for the camera and lenses to aid in keeping them protected. This is not a good choice if you’re looking for a “grab and go” type of backpack. Nice looking, but poor protection.
text_fidelity_b: Case Logic TBC-411 DSLR Compact Backpack (Black)

ESSAGER 100W USBC to USB C Charging Cable with Display, 5A 20V Type-c to Type-c Charging Cable Support Data Transform (Black-2M) This cable works great for confirming the speed that a charger is functioning at. I've tried using apps before but they aren't always accurate. This helped me find a couple of chargers in my stash that don't work as well with my devices as I'd hoped they would. The cord itself is super nice and flexible while the braided sheathing gives it a more premium feel. My only complain is that it would be nice to not only see what wattages a device is pulling but also what voltage/amperage. This would help me to really understand what my chargers are doing and which ones perform as expected. I don't have any devices that will pull 100W over usb, but I could test the cable all the way to 65w and it performed flawlessly.
Overall I really can't complain about a 100W capable cable that works for data and can help me confirm what kind of charge is actually happening

Billboard Bluetooth 5.0 True Wireless Stereo Earbuds with Charging Case, White/Gray (BB2808) I wanted to love these wireless earbuds, but I unfortunately can’t for several reasons.

The sound quality is not good. The description says “extreme bass”, but there is no bass at all.. it’s all treble.
Second of all the bottom metal piece on the one earbuds fell off after one use (in pictures). They still work without that piece, however these are brand new, and broke after 1 use. 😭

The things I do like: The small, convenient charging case. It’s nice and compact. The other thing I do like is the comfort. The design is similar to Apple earbuds and they are comfortable on the ears, even after a long period.

Unfortunately with these, the cons exceed the pros, and I just can’t recommend.
